trimmedBy: node trim-ats-a-captures.mjs (JSON.parse, whole-record selection by posting id, regex redaction of e-mail addresses and separator-bearing phone numbers inside string values, JSON.stringify, prettier); never a byte cut
notes: Second page of the spotify site (skip=50): 40 postings captured, 3 kept; a SHORT page, which is how the end of the board is recognised. OWNERSHIP, EVIDENCE: TEXT_PARTIAL (no employer field in the payload): the same site as spotify-page1 (hostedUrl jobs.lever.co/spotify/<uuid>); the counts (87 of 90 postings name Spotify somewhere) are in that file's notes. All 3 postings that name Spotify nowhere are the 3 kept on this page: 9f66e598-... and 9fd98cde-... (empty main description) and 1f56d4be-... (the Ringer posting). Documented (https://github.com/lever/postings-api): a public read API, HTTPS only, "Only published postings are public ... These jobs may be scraped by third parties"; the only documented rate limit is on application POSTs (not used). robots.txt of both api.lever.co and api.eu.lever.co: User-agent * / Allow: / / Crawl-delay: 1 - a longer gap than the 500 ms proposed in ats-config.ts. The payload carries NO employer name; employer evidence is the posting text naming the employer. Observed drift from the documentation: workplaceType is "onsite" on the live API, the README lists "on-site"; createdAt is present on every posting but is not in the README's field list. E-mail addresses and phone numbers inside string values were replaced by a parser; personal NAMES in free-text descriptions cannot be found by a parser and were not redacted (records were chosen with short descriptions to limit exposure).
